subject: Hosted API pricing — NimTech RFP & competitive comparison
messages:
From: Samira Qureshi <samira@nimtech.com>
To: rachel_kim <rachel_kim@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@nimtech.com
Date: 2026-06-24T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: RFP: Hosted API pricing — request to match competitor per-token rates

Hi Rachel,

Thanks for the quick intro last week. Attached is NimTech's RFP and a short comparison we ran between your hosted API and a couple of other vendors (OpenAI, Anthropic, and our cloud reseller). Our procurement team is asking if Redwood can provide: 1) a per-token price match to the baseline model rates we quoted from OpenAI for non-embedding text generation, and 2) a clear commit-tier schedule (monthly/annual) that reduces unit cost as committed volume increases.

Key asks:
- Target blended per-token goal: $0.0006 (non-embedding) — that’s roughly where OpenAI landed for our projected volume.
- Committed spend: NimTech is prepared to commit $250k/year in exchange for deeper discounting and a review clause at 6 months.
- Contract requirement: standard NimTech security addendum & SOC2 evidence (we have a separate questionnaire forthcoming).

I've attached our RFP (NimTech-RFP-2026-06.pdf). Can you confirm whether Redwood can match or get close to the $0.0006 target with a committed tier? Also please include any SLA or credit language and any onboarding incentives you can offer (credits/consumption windows).

Best,
Samira
Samira Qureshi
Director, Procurement — NimTech

Attachments: NimTech-RFP-2026-06.pdf
From: rachel_kim <rachel_kim@redwood.com>
To: Samira Qureshi <samira@nimtech.com>
Cc: procurement@nimtech.com
Date: 2026-06-24T13:40:00-07:00
Subject: Re: RFP: Hosted API pricing — request to match competitor per-token rates

Hi Samira — thanks for the RFP and the target number. I attached a short proposal and a commit-tier outline (Redwood-HostedAPI-Commit-Pricing-v3.pdf) — summary below.

Quick summary:
- Short answer: we can get materially closer to your target with a committed 12-month agreement and a $200k+ annual spend.
- Counter (proposed): 18% blended price reduction vs list for the base hosted model with a 12-month $200k+ commit, which brings the blended non-embedding per-token to roughly $0.00072 in our example workload.
- Optional escalation: for a $250k/year commit we can extend the match to 20% and provide a one-time $25k onboarding credit and a 60-day extended trial for a subset of high-volume routes.
- SLA: standard enterprise SLA with 99.9% availability and 72-hour incident response for severity 1; credits by percentage of monthly fees.
- Security: we'll attach SOC2 and a short security questionnaire pack right after this thread.

I've also included a simple pricing_model_calc.xlsx so you can see the token math and where incremental volume materially reduces unit cost (prefix caching and batching assumptions included). If you can confirm target commitment (200k vs 250k) I can escalate to pricing to see if we can firm up the 20% match immediately.

Would you be available for a 30-minute call tomorrow to walk through the tiers and the SOC2 evidence?

Best,
Rachel Kim
Senior Account Executive — Redwood Inference

From: NimTech Procurement <procurement@nimtech.com>

Cc: Samira Qureshi <samira@nimtech.com>
Date: 2026-06-25T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: RFP: Hosted API pricing — request to match competitor per-token rates

Rachel — thanks for the rapid reply and the calc. A few notes from procurement: 

- NimTech's internal procurement model is comfortable with $200k/yr if unit economics get to $0.00065 or lower. $0.00072 is still a gap.
- Anthropic quoted a different profile for higher context lengths (we use longer prompts for summaries); their blended was closer to $0.00062 for our expected mix.
- The $250k/year ask was meant to be our starting point for negotiation — if Redwood can hit $0.0006 blended at $250k we can move quickly.

Can you do a follow-up with a more aggressive committed-tier scenario (12 months or 24 months) that shows how Redwood would achieve $0.0006 blended — or alternatively provide a structured rebate/back-credit if actual usage meets the target over the first 6 months?

Thanks,
Procurement (on behalf of Samira)
From: rachel_kim <rachel_kim@redwood.com>
To: ben_carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, evelyn_hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>, aditya_rao <aditya_rao@redwood.com>, jonas_weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-06-26T08:15:00-07:00
Subject: Fwd: NimTech RFP — request for deeper match / internal pricing approval

Team — forwarding NimTech's latest. They want to get to $0.0006 blended at a $250k commit; procurement is pushing for either an upfront committed discount or a retroactive rebate if usage hits targets in 6 months.

My recommendation: we can approve a structured rebate approach instead of moving list price down immediately. Proposed concession (for negotiation):
- Baseline: 18% off list for $200k/yr 12-month commit (as sent).
- Aggressive offer: For $250k/yr 12-month commit, 20% off list plus a structured rebate: if actual usage meets their projected volume thresholds in months 1–6, issue a retro credit equal to the difference to bring blended unit price to $0.00060 (max credit cap $50k).
- Rationale: protects our short-term unit economics while providing NimTech the outcome they asked for; rebate only paid on verified usage tied to mutually agreed telemetry queries.
- Contract additions needed: telemetry logging clause + 6-month review + DocuSign amendment for rebate mechanics.

Evelyn — any objections to the rebate cap and telemetry verification requirement? Ben/Aditya — need help positioning this vs Anthropic and OpenAI in the customer conversation (call planned tomorrow). Jonas — legal signoff on the telemetry clause and rebate wording (I can draft).

Thanks,
Rachel

Subject: Re: RFP: Hosted API pricing — final counter & next steps

Hi Samira / team — appreciated the honest asks and the context on Anthropic/OpenAI. After internal review we've put together a final counter we can stand behind operationally: 

Final offer (summary):
- Commitment: $250,000 per year, 12-month term.
- Price: 20% off public list for the agreed base hosted model, which yields a blended illustrative rate of approximately $0.00068 in our standard workload.
- Performance guarantee: 99.9% availability SLA; 72-hour Sev1 response; credits applied to monthly invoice per SLA schedule.
- Rebate mechanism: If verified usage over the first 6 months meets the projected token thresholds in the RFP, Redwood will issue a one-time retroactive credit (paid on month 7) up to $50,000 to reconcile the blended price down to $0.00060. Verification will use mutually agreed telemetry queries and a short audit window.
- Onboarding: $25,000 onboarding credit; free migration support for two high-volume teams.
- Security: SOC2 bundle attached; we will sign NimTech's standard security addendum with minor redlines (no data retention changes).

Next steps: if you accept, we will send a DocuSign with the commitment addendum and rebate Appendix A. I've included a link to the proposed DocuSign for signature and the HubSpot deal URL for tracking.

DocuSign: https://docusign.com/embdoc?token=XYZ123
HubSpot deal: https://hubspot.com/deal/10234

If you want to discuss the telemetry verification rules I’m happy to hop on a 20-minute call tomorrow. Looking forward to getting NimTech onboarded.

Best,
